column4: Validate AWS Control Tower is deployed and governing both us-east-1 and us-east-2
column5: Control Tower deployment complete and Management account access available
column6:
1. Log in to AWS Console as PlatformAdministrator
2. Navigate to AWS Control Tower dashboard
3. Verify landing zone status shows Enrolled in us-east-1
4. Verify us-east-2 appears as a governed home region
5. Confirm all OUs show green compliance status
column7: Control Tower dashboard shows active governance in both regions with zero drift detected
column14: Prerequisite for all subsequent tests

column4: Validate all seven OUs are created with correct names and nesting under AWS Organizations
column5: Control Tower deployed and AWS Organizations accessible
column6:
1. Navigate to AWS Organizations console
2. Verify Root OU exists
3. Verify child OUs: Security; Infrastructure; Workloads-Prod; Workloads-NonProd; Sandbox; Suspended
4. Confirm no additional unplanned OUs are present
column7: All seven OUs (Root; Security; Infrastructure; Workloads-Prod; Workloads-NonProd; Sandbox; Suspended) exist with correct parent-child relationships
column14: Verify OU nesting matches detailed design Section 4

column4: Validate all required Service Control Policies are attached to the correct OUs
column5: SCPs deployed via Terraform and AWS Organizations console accessible
column6:
1. Navigate to AWS Organizations > Policies > Service Control Policies
2. Verify ins-scp-deny-root is attached at Root OU
3. Verify ins-scp-restrict-regions is attached at Root OU
4. Verify ins-scp-cloudtrail-lock is attached at Root OU
5. Verify ins-scp-mfa-required is attached at Root OU
6. Verify Sandbox OU SCP relaxations are correctly scoped
column7: All four root-level SCPs attached and active; Sandbox OU has reduced SCP set; Suspended OU has deny-all SCP; no SCP attachment errors
column14: Test each SCP individually via IAM Policy Simulator

column4: Validate Resource Control Policy prevents S3 writes to buckets outside the AWS Organization boundary
column5: RCP deployed and test IAM role in member account configured
column6:
1. Assume a member account IAM role via IAM Identity Center
2. Attempt to write an S3 object to an external S3 bucket outside the Organization
3. Attempt to write an S3 object to the internal Log Archive bucket
4. Verify results for both attempts
column7: External S3 write denied with AccessDenied error; internal write blocked by bucket policy as expected; no data exfiltration path exists
column14: Use a dedicated test bucket outside the Org for the external write attempt

column3: IAM Identity Center SSO Login Flow
column4: Validate end-to-end SSO login and cross-account access for all defined permission sets
column5: IAM Identity Center configured and identity source integrated and test users assigned to permission sets
column6:
1. Navigate to IAM Identity Center access portal URL
2. Authenticate as test user with valid MFA
3. Verify account list shows assigned AWS accounts
4. Select PlatformAdministrator role in a Platform account
5. Select WorkloadAdministrator role in a workload account
6. Select SecurityAuditor role across multiple accounts
7. Verify console session starts for each role
column7: SSO portal accessible; MFA prompted and validated; each permission set generates a valid scoped console session; session duration capped at 8 hours
column14: Test all five permission sets: PlatformAdministrator; WorkloadAdministrator; SecurityAuditor; NetworkOperator; FinOps

column4: Validate SCP denies AWS console access when MFA is not registered or is absent
column5: Test IAM Identity Center user without MFA registered and SCP active
column6:
1. Attempt AWS console access with a test user with no MFA device registered
2. Verify SCP evaluation result via CloudTrail
3. Register MFA for the test user
4. Attempt console access again
5. Verify successful access with MFA
column7: Console access denied when MFA is not present; CloudTrail records SCPDenied event; access granted after MFA registration and authentication
column14: Log SCP deny event in CloudTrail for audit evidence

column4: Validate CloudTrail organisation trail delivers management events to Log Archive S3 in both regions
column5: Log Archive S3 bucket provisioned and CloudTrail org trail configured
column6:
1. Perform a test API call in us-east-1 from a member account
2. Perform a test API call in us-east-2 from a member account
3. Wait up to 15 minutes for log delivery
4. Navigate to Log Archive S3 bucket and verify log files present for both regions
5. Validate CloudTrail log file integrity using digest files
column7: CloudTrail log files appear in Log Archive S3 within 15 minutes for both regions; digest file validation confirms no tampering; events include correct accountId and eventSource
column14: Verify S3 Object Lock is active on the Log Archive bucket

column4: Validate AWS Config is recording resource configurations in all accounts and both regions
column5: Config recording enabled via AFT customisation and Log Archive S3 configured as delivery target
column6:
1. Deploy a test security group in a workload account in us-east-1
2. Deploy a test security group in the same account in us-east-2
3. Wait up to 15 minutes for Config snapshot delivery
4. Navigate to AWS Config console in both regions
5. Verify configuration items appear for the test resources
6. Verify Config delivery to Log Archive S3 succeeds
column7: Config recording active in both regions for all accounts; configuration items created within 15 minutes; delivery to Log Archive S3 confirmed; no delivery failures in CloudWatch
column14: Verify using Config delivery channel status page

column4: Validate Log Archive and Audit accounts cannot be accessed by workload administrators
column5: Log Archive and Audit accounts provisioned and SCP and IAM Identity Center assignments configured
column6:
1. Attempt to log in to Log Archive account using WorkloadAdministrator permission set
2. Attempt to log in to Audit account using WorkloadAdministrator permission set
3. Attempt to access Log Archive S3 bucket from a workload account IAM role
4. Log in with PlatformAdministrator and verify access succeeds
column7: WorkloadAdministrator access to Log Archive and Audit accounts denied; PlatformAdministrator and SecurityAuditor access succeeds; no cross-account S3 access from workload roles
column14: Confirms isolation of Security OU per detailed design

column4: Validate complete AFT pipeline execution vends a new account enrolled in Control Tower with all baseline customisations
column5: AFT pipeline deployed and Terraform Cloud workspace active and test account request Terraform file prepared
column6:
1. Commit a new account request .tf file to the AFT account requests repository
2. Monitor CodePipeline execution in the Management account
3. Record start time of pipeline execution
4. Verify CodeBuild stages complete without error
5. Verify new account appears in AWS Organizations and Control Tower
6. Verify AFT customisations applied: spoke VPC; TGW attachment; GuardDuty enrolled; Security Hub enrolled; Budget alerts set; mandatory tags present
7. Record end time and calculate total vending duration
column7: New account vended and enrolled in Control Tower within 30 minutes; all AFT customisations applied; no CodePipeline stage failures
column14: Repeat 3 consecutive times to satisfy go-live success metric per SOW

column4: Validate traffic between two spoke VPCs routes through the Network Hub Network Firewall
column5: Two spoke VPCs attached to TGW and Network Firewall deployed and TGW route tables configured per design
column6:
1. Deploy a test EC2 instance in Spoke VPC A in workload account 1 in us-east-1
2. Deploy a test EC2 instance in Spoke VPC B in workload account 2 in us-east-1
3. Send ICMP traffic from Instance A to Instance B
4. Capture VPC Flow Logs and Network Firewall alert logs
5. Verify traffic traverses the Network Firewall endpoint
6. Verify spoke-to-spoke traffic follows the Inspection Route Table path
column7: Traffic between spoke VPCs routes through Network Firewall endpoint in Network Hub VPC; VPC Flow Logs confirm inspection path; permitted traffic forwarded; denied traffic logged in Firewall alert logs
column14: Repeat with east-west deny test to verify default-deny firewall stance

column4: Validate internet-bound egress from spoke VPCs routes through the centralised NAT Gateway in the Network Hub account
column5: Spoke VPC deployed and TGW and NAT Gateway configured and no Internet Gateway in spoke VPC
column6:
1. Deploy a test EC2 instance in a spoke VPC with no Internet Gateway
2. Attempt an outbound HTTPS request to a public internet endpoint
3. Verify the source IP of the outbound request matches the NAT Gateway Elastic IP
4. Verify the traffic appears in Network Firewall north-south logs
column7: Internet egress succeeds; source IP matches centralised NAT Gateway EIP not a spoke-VPC address; traffic recorded in Network Firewall north-south logs; spoke VPC has no direct internet path
column14: Confirms no internet gateway bypass possible in spoke accounts

column4: Validate VPN tunnel establishment and routing between Network Hub account and on-premises gateway in both regions
column5: On-premises gateway configured and VPN connections created in Network Hub account for both regions
column6:
1. Verify both VPN tunnels in us-east-1 show UP status in AWS Console
2. Verify both VPN tunnels in us-east-2 show UP status
3. Verify BGP routes are propagated on both tunnels
4. Send test traffic from a spoke VPC to an on-premises test host
5. Verify on-premises route table shows AWS CIDR blocks via VPN
column7: Both VPN tunnels UP in both regions; BGP routes propagated; test traffic reaches on-premises host from AWS spoke VPC; baseline latency documented
column14: Document baseline latency for DR planning; test tunnel failover procedure

column4: Validate Security Hub is enabled in all accounts with FSBP standard and findings aggregate to Audit account
column5: Security Hub enabled via AFT customisation and Audit account configured as delegated administrator
column6:
1. Log in to Audit account as SecurityAuditor
2. Navigate to Security Hub > Summary
3. Verify FSBP standard is active for all member accounts
4. Verify findings from all member accounts aggregate in the Audit account
5. Record overall FSBP compliance score
6. Verify zero CRITICAL findings in Production and Platform accounts
column7: Security Hub FSBP active in all accounts; findings aggregate from all accounts and both regions to Audit account; FSBP compliance score >= 80% at go-live; zero CRITICAL findings in Production and Platform accounts
column14: Hard go-live gate; score below 80% blocks go-live

column4: Validate GuardDuty is enabled in all accounts and both regions with the Audit account as delegated administrator
column5: GuardDuty enabled via AFT and delegated administrator configured in Audit account
column6:
1. Log in to Audit account as SecurityAuditor
2. Navigate to GuardDuty > Accounts
3. Verify all member accounts show Enabled in us-east-1
4. Verify all member accounts show Enabled in us-east-2
5. Verify Audit account is the delegated administrator
6. Generate a test finding and verify it appears in the Audit account
column7: GuardDuty active org-wide in both regions; all accounts show Enabled status; Audit account is delegated admin; test finding visible in Audit account console within 5 minutes
column14: Verify SNS alert fires for High-severity test finding

column4: Validate that Terraform drift detection identifies any manual console change in a Production account
column5: A Production workload account provisioned and Terraform state current and CI/CD pipeline active
column6:
1. Note the current Terraform state for a production security group resource
2. Manually modify the security group via AWS Console to add an inbound rule
3. Run terraform plan against the production workspace
4. Verify terraform plan shows the manual change as drift
5. Revert the change via terraform apply
6. Confirm production state matches IaC configuration
column7: Terraform plan detects drift; drift alert raised; IaC state is authoritative and re-apply corrects the drift; zero manual changes remain after apply
column14: Confirms >= 95% IaC coverage requirement; perform in NonProd OU first

column4: Validate AFT pipeline vends a guardrail-enrolled account in under 30 minutes across three consecutive test runs
column5: AFT pipeline deployed and Terraform Cloud workspace active and three distinct test account request files prepared
column6:
1. Commit test account request file #1 to AFT account requests repo
2. Record exact pipeline start time from CodePipeline
3. Monitor all pipeline stages to completion
4. Record end time and calculate elapsed duration for Run 1
5. Repeat steps 1-4 for test account request files #2 and #3
6. Document elapsed time for each run
column7: All three consecutive runs complete in under 30 minutes; zero pipeline failures across all three runs; results documented in Test Results Report
column14: Hard go-live gate per SOW success metrics; any run over 30 min is a failure

column4: Measure baseline Network Firewall throughput in both regions and document for capacity planning
column5: Network Firewall deployed in us-east-1 and us-east-2 and test EC2 instances in spoke VPCs
column6:
1. Deploy two test EC2 instances in separate spoke VPCs in us-east-1 with traffic routed through firewall
2. Run iPerf3 sustained throughput test for 5 minutes
3. Record throughput and packet rate and drop count from Network Firewall metrics
4. Repeat test in us-east-2
5. Document baseline metrics in Network Testing Report
column7: Baseline throughput measured and documented; Network Firewall drop rate equals zero for permitted traffic; results documented for future workload capacity planning
column14: Baseline documentation only; no hard pass/fail throughput threshold for this test

column4: Measure and document baseline latency between us-east-1 and us-east-2 via TGW inter-region peering
column5: TGW inter-region peering active and test instances in both regions
column6:
1. Deploy test EC2 instances in Network Hub VPCs in us-east-1 and us-east-2
2. Run continuous ping test for 5 minutes across TGW inter-region peering
3. Record average and minimum and maximum and 95th percentile round-trip latency
4. Document results in Network Testing Report
column7: Latency baseline documented; typical us-east-1 to us-east-2 inter-region latency expected below 20ms; results used as DR failover planning baseline
column14: Baseline documentation only; no hard latency threshold for this test

column4: Validate CloudTrail delivers management events to Log Archive S3 within 15 minutes of the API call
column5: CloudTrail org trail active and Log Archive S3 configured and CloudWatch metric for log delivery active
column6:
1. Record current timestamp T0
2. Execute a test API call in a member account
3. Monitor S3 Log Archive bucket for new log file delivery
4. Record timestamp T1 when log file containing the test event appears
5. Calculate delivery latency as T1 minus T0
6. Repeat 5 times at different times of day
column7: CloudTrail log delivery latency under 15 minutes for all 5 test runs; average latency documented; CloudWatch metric shows no delivery failures
column14: Part of Log Archive SLA validation; 15-minute RPO depends on this test

column4: Validate SCP prevents root account actions across all member accounts
column5: Root credentials sealed in Secrets Manager and SCP ins-scp-deny-root active at Root OU
column6:
1. In a test member account attempt to perform an action using root account credentials
2. Verify the action is denied by SCP
3. Review CloudTrail for the SCPDenied error
4. Verify the denial event is logged with correct errorCode and errorMessage
column7: Root account actions in all member accounts denied by SCP; CloudTrail records SCPDenied event for each attempt; no root-initiated resource changes succeed
column14: Use a dedicated test account in NonProd OU; do not test in Production

column4: Validate SCP prevents API calls to AWS regions other than us-east-1 and us-east-2
column5: SCP ins-scp-restrict-regions active and test IAM Identity Center user available
column6:
1. Assume a WorkloadAdministrator role in a test member account
2. Attempt to create a resource in us-west-2
3. Attempt to create a resource in eu-west-1
4. Attempt to create a resource in us-east-1 which should succeed
5. Verify CloudTrail shows SCPDenied for us-west-2 and eu-west-1 attempts
column7: API calls to all regions except us-east-1 and us-east-2 denied by SCP; CloudTrail SCPDenied events recorded for all out-of-region attempts; us-east-1 resource creation succeeds
column14: Critical for US data residency compliance requirement

column3: SCP CloudTrail and Config Lock Enforcement
column4: Validate SCP prevents disabling of CloudTrail or Config recording in any member account
column5: SCP ins-scp-cloudtrail-lock active and CloudTrail and Config recording active in member accounts
column6:
1. Assume a WorkloadAdministrator role in a test member account
2. Attempt to stop the CloudTrail trail via StopLogging API
3. Attempt to delete the CloudTrail trail via DeleteTrail API
4. Attempt to stop Config recording via StopConfigurationRecorder API
5. Verify all attempts are denied by SCP
column7: CloudTrail stop and delete and Config stop actions all denied by SCP for non-PlatformAdministrator roles; CloudTrail records SCPDenied events; logging remains uninterrupted
column14: Evidence for SOC 2 CC7.2 audit logging requirement

column3: S3 Log Archive Object Lock Validation
column4: Validate S3 Object Lock prevents deletion or modification of CloudTrail log files within the retention period
column5: Log Archive S3 bucket with Object Lock compliance mode active and CloudTrail log files present
column6:
1. Identify a CloudTrail log file in the Log Archive S3 bucket
2. Attempt to delete the log file using PlatformAdministrator credentials
3. Attempt to overwrite the log file with modified content
4. Verify the Object Lock retention date on the file confirms 90-day minimum
column7: Log file deletion denied with Object Lock compliance mode error; file overwrite denied; Object Lock expiry date confirms 90-day minimum retention; MFA-Delete active on bucket
column14: Satisfies SOC 2; HIPAA; and NIST 800-53 AU-9 audit trail immutability requirement

column3: Encryption at Rest and in Transit Validation
column4: Validate all Log Archive S3 data is encrypted at rest and all API communication is TLS-encrypted
column5: Log Archive S3 configured and CloudTrail delivering logs
column6:
1. Inspect Log Archive S3 bucket default encryption settings
2. Verify SSE-S3 AES-256 is enforced as default encryption
3. Check S3 bucket policy for aws:SecureTransport condition
4. Attempt an HTTP non-TLS PUT request to the S3 bucket
5. Verify EBS volumes in shared accounts have encryption-by-default via Config rule
column7: S3 bucket shows SSE-S3 encryption active; aws:SecureTransport condition rejects all HTTP requests; Config rule ec2-ebs-encryption-by-default shows COMPLIANT for all shared accounts
column14: Verify KMS key rotation enabled for all customer-managed keys

column3: IAM Access Analyser No External Access Findings
column4: Validate IAM Access Analyser reports zero external-access findings in Production and Platform accounts
column5: IAM Access Analyser enabled in all accounts via Security Hub FSBP and Audit account aggregation active
column6:
1. Navigate to IAM Access Analyser in Audit account
2. Review all findings across Production and Platform account zones of trust
3. Verify no external-access findings exist for resources accessible from outside the Organisation
4. Document any findings in NonProd or Sandbox for risk acceptance
column7: Zero external-access findings in Production and Platform accounts; any findings in NonProd or Sandbox documented and risk-accepted by Client Security Lead
column14: External-access findings reduce FSBP compliance score

column4: Validate Network Firewall continues to pass traffic when one Availability Zone endpoint becomes unavailable
column5: Network Firewall deployed in two AZs per region and traffic flowing through both AZ endpoints
column6:
1. Record baseline spoke-to-spoke traffic throughput through the firewall
2. Simulate AZ-a endpoint failure by modifying the TGW route table to remove the AZ-a firewall endpoint
3. Verify traffic re-routes to AZ-b firewall endpoint
4. Measure time to re-route and traffic interruption duration
5. Restore AZ-a routing and verify traffic returns to dual-AZ distribution
column7: Traffic re-routes to surviving AZ endpoint within 30 minutes; zero traffic loss after route reconvergence; Network Firewall metrics show no sustained drop rate increase; restoration to dual-AZ succeeds
column14: Test in us-east-1; repeat in us-east-2; document actual failover time

column3: IaC Landing Zone Rebuild RTO Validation
column4: Validate the landing zone can be rebuilt from Terraform state and AFT configuration within 4 hours
column5: All Terraform workspaces in a known clean state and Terraform Cloud accessible and AFT repo available
column6:
1. In a non-production test account simulate a component failure by destroying a defined resource subset via terraform destroy
2. Record start time
3. Execute terraform apply from current Terraform state to rebuild destroyed resources
4. Verify all resources recreated and healthy
5. Record end time and calculate elapsed duration
column7: Complete resource rebuild from IaC state completes within 4 hours; all rebuilt resources match the current Terraform configuration; no manual intervention required; elapsed time documented
column14: Test against a representative resource subset; full org rebuild is theoretical

column4: Validate S3 CRR replicates Log Archive objects from us-east-1 to us-east-2 within the RPO target
column5: S3 CRR configured on Log Archive bucket and us-east-2 replica bucket active
column6:
1. Deliver a test CloudTrail log file to the us-east-1 Log Archive S3 bucket
2. Record the delivery timestamp
3. Monitor the us-east-2 replica bucket for the replicated object
4. Record the replication completion timestamp
5. Calculate replication lag
column7: Log Archive objects replicated from us-east-1 to us-east-2 within 15 minutes; replication lag documented; Object Lock settings preserved on replicated objects
column14: Verify Object Lock compliance mode is maintained on the us-east-2 replica

column4: Validate per-account AWS Budget alerts fire at 80% and 100% spend thresholds for all accounts
column5: AWS Budgets configured via AFT customisation on all accounts and SNS alerting topic active
column6:
1. Log in to Management account as PlatformAdministrator
2. Navigate to AWS Budgets for a test workload account
3. Verify a budget exists with 80% threshold alert configured
4. Verify a budget exists with 100% threshold alert configured
5. Verify SNS topic is assigned as the alert notification target
6. Verify alert notification email is configured on the SNS topic
column7: 80% and 100% budget alerts exist for all accounts; SNS topic correctly associated; email recipient confirmed; alert notification test delivery succeeds
column14: Verify all vended accounts have Budget alerts as part of go-live checklist

column3: CloudWatch SNS Alert Routing for Critical Findings
column4: Validate EventBridge rules route Security Hub CRITICAL and GuardDuty High-severity findings to SNS with email delivery
column5: Security Hub and GuardDuty and EventBridge rules and SNS topic deployed in Audit account

2. Monitor EventBridge rule for finding match

column14: Confirms go-live readiness for P1 incident escalation path

column14: Verify IPAM pool utilisation is reported correctly; address-space exhaustion testing is out of scope
